Its products include the Agri Credit Line (recurring capital to restock inputs), Agri Supplier Financing (invoice financing), Agri Buyer Financing (deferred-payment terms), and Stockist Financing (direct distributor payments). The public site is built on Wix and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint plus an llms.txt file for agentic AI access, though Avenews does not publish a bespoke developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-connected portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Kampi
providers.description: Kampi is an aquaculture technology company headquartered in Samborondón, Ecuador, building an AI-powered mobile app and platform for real-time shrimp farm management. Created by the team behind XpertSea (KAMPI AQUA SOLUTIONS S.A. / XpertSea Solution Inc.), Kampi converts daily farm records into personalized guidance using machine learning, an approach it calls dynamic precision farming. The platform combines three integrated tools — Pond Vision (intelligent pond monitoring), FarmAI (predictive biomass analytics) and Farmbook (digital team integration) — to deliver biomass monitoring, biological parameter tracking, real-time alerts, harvest planning and FCR optimization from a smartphone, online or offline. Kampi is a marketing-and-mobile-app company with no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its published web presence and a verbatim llms.txt it serves.

providers.name: Hippo Harvest
providers.description: Hippo Harvest is a controlled-environment agriculture company based in Pescadero, California, founded in 2019, that grows USDA-certified-organic leafy greens in modular greenhouses run by custom autonomous mobile robots and machine learning. Its closed-loop, direct-to-root watering and nutrient system is published by the company as using 92% less water, 55% less fertilizer and 94% less land than conventional field agriculture, while pricing to compete with field-grown product. Hippo Harvest sells packaged salad greens (spring mix, spinach, 50/50 blend, butter lettuce) into grocery retail rather than selling software: the robotics, computer vision and growing-control stack is internal operating infrastructure, not a product. It raised a $21M Series B led by Standard Investments in February 2024 and a $30M Series C led by Cox Farms in July 2026, and is permitting a 30-acre facility in Hollister, California. No public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind was found on any host the company controls.

providers.name: AGTools
providers.description: Agtools, Inc. is an agricultural technology (AgTech) company providing a real-time data analytics and market-intelligence SaaS platform for the global food supply chain. The platform aggregates and curates hundreds of official government, institutional, university, and weather data sources covering 450+ specialty crops and commodities across 189+ countries, exposing 70+ variables and 25+ years of historical records (pricing, supply, demand, exchange rates, weather, CO2 footprint, and transportation costs) through dashboards, daily commodity reports, and a price analyzer so growers, shippers, buyers, and retailers can forecast demand, manage purchase orders, and reduce food waste. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Irvine, California, Agtools is a Techstars Farm to Fork alumnus and Microsoft Machine Learning & AI award winner. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface has been published to date.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel (Apeel Sciences) is a food technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Goleta, California. It produces a plant-derived, edible coating, made from lipids and glycerolipids found in the peels, seeds and pulp of produce, that is applied to fresh fruit and vegetables at packing houses to slow water loss and oxidation, extending shelf life and reducing food waste across the supply chain. Apeel-treated produce is sold through grocery retailers in multiple countries. In 2021 Apeel acquired ImpactVision and added hyperspectral imaging to its supplier installations to grade interior quality, ripeness and freshness. Apeel is a materials-science and supply-chain operator: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer sign-up.

providers.name: Eat Just
providers.description: Eat Just, Inc. is a food technology company founded in 2011 by Josh Tetrick and Josh Balk, headquartered in Alameda, California, that makes plant-based alternatives to animal products. Its flagship product is JUST Egg, a liquid and folded plant-based egg made from mung bean protein, alongside JUST Meat, JUST Protein and JUST condiments. Its GOOD Meat subsidiary produces cultivated chicken and in December 2020 became the first company in the world to receive regulatory approval to sell cultivated meat, in Singapore, followed by US FDA and USDA approval in June 2023. The company sells through retail, foodservice, restaurant and industrial channels in North America and Europe. Eat Just publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; this profile records its public web and corporate surface only.

providers.name: Moleaer
providers.description: Moleaer Inc. is a Hawthorne, California nanobubble technology company that designs and manufactures nanobubble generators — Clear, Bloom, Lotus, Neo, Nexus, Trinity, Freya, Indalo, Titan and XTB, plus the NanoShield service — used to raise dissolved oxygen, act as a chemical-free oxidant, and control algae and biofilm in aquaculture, horticulture and irrigation water, lakes and ponds, wastewater treatment, food and beverage, car washes, mining, and oil and gas. Its only digital surface is a customer-only remote monitoring service, launched in 2020 with industrial IoT provider AMI Global, that reports equipment status and water-quality readings (DO, pH, ORP, temperature, conductivity) into a login-gated portal at www.monitoring-moleaer.com. Moleaer publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification; equipment-level integration is offered through industrial control protocols (SCADA/Modbus/EtherNet-IP) on the generators themselves, not through a web API.

providers.name: Sioma
providers.description: SIOMA is a Colombian precision-agriculture (agtech) software platform for tropical crops such as oil palm, banana, and cacao. It helps plantations monitor field labor, track harvest and weighing (pesaje) operations with GPS, and make data-driven decisions to raise productivity. The product combines a mobile field-management app, GPS-based labor tracking, smart weighing hardware (Nukak, Sigma, Jaco, and Bascula-G scales), and Siomi, an AI assistant for agriculture. SIOMA is delivered as a customer web and mobile application and is backed by 500 Global. No public API or developer program is currently published.

providers.name: Verdant Robotics
providers.description: Verdant Robotics is an agricultural robotics company building precision farming systems for specialty crop growers. Its flagship SharpShooter uses "Aim & Apply" technology - machine learning and computer vision that identify crops and weeds in real time, build a three-dimensional map of the field, and deliver microliter-precise applications directly onto weeds without contacting the crop, doing over 240 targeted applications per second. The Robotics-as-a- Service platform reduces herbicide use by up to 99% and manual labor costs by up to 85% across carrots, leafy greens, cabbage, onions, and grass seed and sod production. Founded by leaders from the self-driving vehicle industry and commercial agriculture, Verdant is backed by DCVC. This profile was surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company; Verdant publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation - its GitHub organization hosts robotics tooling and forks (cbuf message serialization, Jetson build scripts, YOLO/ultralytics forks) rather than a product API.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: mPower Social
providers.description: mPower Social Enterprises Ltd. is a Dhaka, Bangladesh technology-for-development company founded in 2008 by Harvard and MIT graduate students as ClickDiagnostics — winner of the MIT $100K competition — and renamed after moving its center of gravity to Bangladesh in 2010. mPower designs, builds and operates information systems for governments, UN agencies, donor organizations and international NGOs across health and nutrition, water and sanitation, agriculture and livestock, education, governance and rights, livelihood and poverty alleviation, climate and environment, and humanitarian response, and states it has deployed more than 300 ICT solutions across 17 countries in the Global South. Its engineering practice is built on open-source digital public goods — DHIS2, OpenMRS, OpenSRP / FHIR Core, Bahmni and Moodle — which it customizes, integrates and supports for national health management information systems, electronic medical records and shared health records, rather than shipping a hosted product of its own. The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified. mPower publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract; its public software surface is a GitHub organization made up largely of downstream forks of the open-source health platforms it implements, plus a set of first-party Android apps on Google Play.

providers.name: PharmaCann
providers.description: PharmaCann is one of the largest vertically integrated cannabis companies in the United States, founded in 2014 and operating cultivation centers, processing facilities and retail dispensaries across eight states — Colorado, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New York, Ohio and Pennsylvania. The company runs nine cultivation and processing facilities (Denver CO, Dwight IL, Lothian and Stevensville MD, Holliston MA, Warren MI, Hamptonburgh NY, Buckeye Lake OH and Olyphant PA) and sells through two retail banners, LivWell (Colorado and Michigan) and Verilife (Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New York, Ohio and Pennsylvania), alongside a house of product brands including Matter, Magnitude, Full Melt, CAM, P3, LivWell Flower, Hash and PC Nursery. PharmaCann is a physical-goods operator in a federally restricted, state-regulated industry; it publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AgFunder
providers.description: AgFunder is a global agrifood-tech venture capital firm investing in deeptech and foundational technologies across AI, biology, robotics, and climate to advance food, agriculture, and human and planetary health. Founded roughly a decade ago by Michael Dean and Rob Leclerc and headquartered in Silicon Valley with offices in London and Singapore, the firm manages over $300M in assets and has backed more than 100 portfolio companies across four continents. AgFunder also operates AgFunderNews (AFN), the leading agtech and foodtech news and research publication, and publishes market research for the agrifoodtech ecosystem. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the firm's public identity and site properties; AgFunder publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Agtonomy
providers.description: Agtonomy is a physical-AI and automation software company, founded in 2021 by growers and technologists, that embeds machine vision, connectivity, and AI directly into agricultural and off-road equipment from manufacturers such as Bobcat, Kubota, and Clemens. Its platform combines GPS guidance, computer vision, and fleet intelligence so a single operator can plan, remotely monitor, and review autonomous tasks like mowing, hauling, spraying, and cultivation across 10+ tractors at once. The TeleFarmer product controls these field missions through an intuitive app, helping growers address labor shortages and rising operational costs. Backed by investors including GV and Allison Transmission, Agtonomy operates primarily across the western United States with expansion into the Southeast US and Australia. This profile was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agtonomy publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel Sciences is a food technology company headquartered in Santa Barbara, California that develops plant-based protective coatings which extend the shelf life of fresh fruits and vegetables. The company uses food-grade ingredients derived from the peels, pulp, and seeds of plants to create a thin, edible layer that reinforces produce's natural peel, slowing water loss and oxidation. This extends peak taste, juiciness, and nutrient retention while reducing reliance on refrigeration, waxes, pesticides, and plastic packaging across the fresh-produce supply chain. Apeel positions itself as a sustainability and food-waste leader, reporting that since 2021 its technology has prevented millions of pieces of fruit from spoiling, avoided tens of thousands of metric tons of CO2-equivalent emissions, and conserved billions of liters of water. Its products have undergone regulatory review in the United States, European Union, and other markets. Apeel is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Bluewhite (fka Blue White Robotics)
providers.description: Bluewhite (formerly Blue White Robotics) is an autonomy company that builds an AI-powered "Field Intelligence" physical-AI engine for operating vehicles in demanding, unstructured, real-world environments. Founded in Israel, the company first commercialized autonomous agriculture — retrofitting existing tractor fleets with an aftermarket autonomy kit for driverless spraying, mowing, and other field operations — and has since extended the same edge-processing autonomy stack to defense and security missions through OEM integrations and complete unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). Bluewhite is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this API Evangelist profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Elevarm
providers.description: Elevarm is an upstream-focused agritech company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Bandung, Indonesia, that elevates smallholder horticulture farmers across West Java, Central Java, and Yogyakarta. It aggregates and supports more than 15,000 farmers with high-quality inputs (premium greenhouse seedlings, bio-based fertilizers, and environmentally friendly pest control via its NextBio line), lab-based soil testing through Klinik Tani, an AI-powered farming productivity app for land monitoring and data-driven agronomy recommendations, pro-farmer financing, and the PasarAgri commodity trading platform that links supply to business buyers. Elevarm is backed by Intudo, Insignia Ventures Partners, and 500 Global.

providers.name: Elo Life
providers.description: Elo Life Systems is a next-generation food and agriculture company based in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, using molecular farming and gene-editing to turn high-yield crops into biofactories for natural food ingredients. Its lead product is a low-calorie, high-potency natural sweetener inspired by monk fruit that is designed to taste like sugar while replacing both sugar and artificial sweeteners at a lower cost. Elo also partners with Dole to develop a fungus-resistant (TR4/Fusarium wilt) Cavendish banana. Backed by DCVC Bio and Novo Holdings, the company raised an oversubscribed $20.5M Series A2 to scale its molecular-farming platform. Elo Life is a food-tech / agricultural-biotech company and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Enough
providers.description: ENOUGH (brand name ABUNDA) is a food-technology company that produces mycoprotein through a zero-waste fermentation process, growing fungi on grain-derived sugars. Operating as a B2B ingredient supplier to retailers and food brands, ENOUGH makes nutrient-dense, sustainable meat and seafood alternatives — including burgers, chicken-style products, noodles, and snacks — that use dramatically less water and produce far less CO2 than conventional animal protein. The company operates one of the world's largest mycoprotein fermentation facilities and is backed by DCVC. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; ENOUGH is a food-ingredient business and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Freight Farms
providers.description: Freight Farms is a Boston-based vertical farming company that builds the Greenery container farm, a commercial-scale, modular, hydroponic farm assembled inside a shipping container so growers can produce hyper-local produce 365 days a year in any climate. Its Farmhand software platform provides remote farm control, farm data analytics and insights, crop planning, and pre-set growing recipes, backed by certified training, onboarding, logistics, and technical support. The company reports 800+ farms across 50 U.S. states and 3 territories and 2,100+ farmers in 42 countries. Freight Farms currently publishes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI surface; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, brand, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe while a programmatic surface is monitored for.

providers.name: MycoTechnology
providers.description: MycoTechnology, Inc. is a Colorado-based food ingredient technology company that uses mushroom mycelial fermentation to create naturally derived ingredients for the food and beverage industry. Operating publicly as Myco (mycoiq.com), the company develops and manufactures flavor-modulation and sweetening ingredients — ClearIQ natural flavor, ClearHT natural flavor, and Zukora honey truffle sweet protein — used for bitterness masking, off-note mitigation, sugar reduction, and clean-label formulation in plant proteins, meat analogues, dairy alternatives, and health and wellness products. It also offers Fermentation as a Service (FaaS) and a MyCulinary culinary science program for food brands. This is an ingredient manufacturing and food science business, not a software or API company: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Stellapps
providers.description: Stellapps is an end-to-end dairy technology company from Bangalore, India (IIT Madras incubated, founded 2011) that digitizes milk production, milk procurement, and cold-chain management through its SmartMoo full-stack IoT platform. Sensors in milking systems, animal wearables, chilling equipment, and procurement peripherals stream data to the SmartMoo Big Data Cloud for analytics and machine learning serving dairy farmers, cooperatives, and processors, with applications including mooON herd management, smartAMCU and smartCC milk procurement, ConTrak cold-chain monitoring, mooFlow ERP, and mooPay financial services. Stellapps publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; the SmartMoo platform is accessed through hosted applications behind CAS single sign-on.

providers.name: CF Industries Holdings
providers.description: CF Industries Holdings is a Fortune 500 American manufacturer and distributor of nitrogen-based fertilizers (ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, UAN) and clean-energy products serving agricultural and industrial customers worldwide. CF operates one of the largest global ammonia production networks and is scaling clean (blue and green) ammonia for low-carbon energy. CF does not publish a public developer API program; programmatic data access is limited to investor-relations SEC filings feeds, press/news RSS, and partner EDI/B2B integrations with agricultural distributors, rail, terminal, and industrial customers.

providers.name: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd
providers.description: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd (JISL) is a global agri-industrial conglomerate headquartered in Jalgaon, Maharashtra, India, and is widely cited as the world's largest micro-irrigation company. Founded in 1963 by Padma Shri recipient Bhavarlal Jain under the slogan "More Crop Per Drop," the company manufactures drip and sprinkler irrigation systems, PVC/HDPE/PP and plumbing piping, rigid and foam plastic sheets, solar pumping and photovoltaic systems, tissue-culture planting material, greenhouses and protected cultivation, and processed foods. JISL operates 33 manufacturing bases across four continents, serves 126+ countries through 11,000+ dealers, is listed on the BSE and NSE, and reports turnover exceeding USD 1.2 billion. The company publishes a structured llms.txt for AI crawlers but exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Benson Hill *
providers.description: Benson Hill (now operating as Confluence Genetics at confluence.ag) is a seed-innovation company that develops high-protein, energy-dense soybean varieties using AI-driven plant science and advanced crop genetics. Its soy solutions serve three markets — animal feed, human food, and renewable fuel — pairing proven genetics with technology and environmental responsibility. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; the company has since rebranded from Benson Hill to Confluence Genetics and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Karnott
providers.description: Karnott is a French agricultural technology company based in Lille that builds connected tracking devices and a digital management platform for farms, equipment cooperatives (CUMA), agricultural contractors (ETA), and wine growers. Its beacon automatically records equipment usage and field interventions without manual data entry, enabling real-time fleet and equipment monitoring, fuel-cost tracking, parcel mapping, and precise billing and regulatory documentation. Karnott is a portfolio company of Partech. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found on the provider's public surface as of this pass.

providers.name: GOOD Meat
providers.description: GOOD Meat is the cultivated-meat division of Eat Just, Inc., a San Francisco food technology company. It grows real chicken from animal cells in production bioreactors rather than by raising and slaughtering birds, and it was the first company in the world cleared to sell cultivated meat to consumers — approved in Singapore in December 2020, then cleared by the U.S. FDA in March 2023 and granted USDA label approval and grant of inspection in June 2023. Its products have been served at 1880 and Huber's Butchery in Singapore and at José Andrés' China Chilcano in Washington, D.C., and in May 2024 it became the first cultivated meat sold at retail. GOOD Meat is a consumer packaged-food and foodservice brand: it sells meat, not software. It operates no developer program, publishes no API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification, and its parent's GitHub organization carries no public repositories.

providers.name: Finres
providers.description: Finres (finres SAS) is a French climate-risk analytics company building a decision platform for agriculture. It translates climate hazards into economic consequences for farms, agricultural value chains and territories, combining agronomic, pedological, climate and market data with AI models that are peer-reviewed and validated against published research. Two productized offerings sit on top of the platform - a farm-level economic and climate viability diagnostic (DPEC, currently in beta, seeded from a grower's TelePAC parcel file and reference datasets such as Agreste, IPPAP and RICA) and bespoke territorial or sector studies. Finres was founded by Florent Baarsch, previously with the World Bank, the United Nations and climate research institutes, and its customers include the French government, the World Bank, the Green Climate Fund, IFAD and the FAO. The company markets high-resolution data delivery into customer decision systems, but as of this enrichment pass publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification or SDK - access is arranged through a sales demo.

providers.name: Hexafarms
providers.description: Hexafarms GmbH is a Berlin-based agricultural technology company that builds AI-powered greenhouse optimization software for commercial growers. Its platform combines computer vision, environmental sensors, and machine learning to help greenhouse and foil-tunnel operations forecast yield, register crops, and detect pests and disease early. Products include AI yield forecasting (claimed up to 20% more accurate than traditional methods), automated crop registration via fruit and flower counting, pest and disease monitoring, and environmental sensing across crops such as strawberries, tomatoes, bell peppers, blueberries, cucumbers, raspberries, and aubergine. The product is delivered as a login-gated web application at hexafarms.app; no public developer API or documentation surface has been identified. Hexafarms was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Better Origin
providers.description: Better Origin is a UK-based agritech company decarbonizing the food chain by converting food waste into sustainable, locally produced animal feed. Its core technology is a fully automated, AI-controlled containerized insect farm that breeds black soldier fly larvae to consume food waste and produce nutrient-rich insect-based ingredients for pet food, poultry feed, and aquaculture. The systems are remotely monitored and controlled by software and require no specialist knowledge from operators. Better Origin is a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Kula Bio
providers.description: Kula Bio is an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Natick, Massachusetts that manufactures Kula-N, a nitrogen-fixing microbial biofertilizer built on the bacterium Xanthobacter autotrophicus. The company's process, originating in Dr. Dan Nocera's research, "supercharges" the microbe with renewable energy so it fixes atmospheric nitrogen at the root zone, letting growers replace a portion of synthetic nitrogen while cutting the greenhouse-gas footprint of the applied product. Kula Bio sells a liquid formulation and, since February 2026, a Soluble Powder (SP) line, serving produce and row-crop growers through agronomic distribution rather than through software. It raised a $50M Series A led by Lowercarbon Capital and was named to TIME's list of America's Top GreenTech Companies of 2026. Kula Bio publishes no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind; this profile records that measured absence alongside its verified public corporate surface.

providers.name: Plantible Foods
providers.description: Plantible Foods is a business-to-business food-ingredient company founded in 2018 by Dutch entrepreneurs Tony and Maurits, with its first commercial production facility in Schleicher County, Texas. The company cultivates lemna (duckweed) in controlled, automated aquafarms and uses a proprietary water-based extraction process to isolate RuBisCO, sold as Rubi Protein — roughly 85% protein by weight with a PDCAAS of 1.0 — alongside Lemna Leaf Greens and application-specific systems such as RubiWhisk and RubiPrime. It sells to food manufacturers and ingredient companies rather than consumers, and in February 2026 became the first company to receive an FDA "no questions" GRAS letter for isolated RuBisCO protein in food. Investors include RA Capital, Nourish Ventures, Chipotle, Kellogg's and CJ Group. Plantible is an agricultural manufacturing business: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and plantiblefoods.com is a Webflow marketing site with no developer surface.

providers.name: Agro Club
providers.description: Agro.Club is a US-based agtech company operating a digital grain trading and crop marketing marketplace that connects farmers with grain buyers. The platform offers competitive bids for corn, wheat, soybeans and other grains, along with logistics (truck and rail transportation), quality control, financing, and market insights. Farmers can transact through cash, FOB or delivered, and basis contracts, plus a Firm Offer price-target monitoring service. Agro.Club serves tens of thousands of farmers and grain companies across the largest agricultural hubs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. Agro.Club does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation; its api.agro.club host is a private backend that serves the company's own applications.

providers.name: Farmwise
providers.description: FarmWise Labs is an agricultural technology company building AI-powered robotics for specialty crop farming. Its flagship product, Vulcan, is an intra-row weeder and precision cultivator that uses computer vision and machine learning to identify and mechanically remove weeds without herbicides, covering up to three acres per hour and saving growers an estimated $250+ per acre. The self-calibrating machine operates in all field conditions and receives over-the-air software updates. Founded in San Francisco and backed by GV (Google Ventures), FarmWise is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.

providers.name: Farm Service Agency
providers.description: As directed by the OPEN (Open, Public, Electronic, and Necessary) Government Data Act and through its commitment to United States agriculturalists and interested public, FSA provides numerous data resources through reports, visualizations, and other formats.

providers.name: Agrapp
providers.description: Agrapp is a Chilean agricultural technology (AgTech) company offering "el cuaderno de campo inteligente" (the intelligent field notebook) — a mobile and web SaaS platform that helps small and medium farmers record, track, and manage their field operations without complex spreadsheets. Founded in 2016 in Santiago and backed by 500 Global, Start-Up Chile, OpenBeauchef, and ChileGlobal Ventures, the platform provides labor and task tracking with per-task cost analysis, inventory and supply (bodega) control, a work calendar, worker attendance and performance monitoring, WhatsApp and email alerts, and agricultural plus financial reporting to support data-driven decisions. It runs on iOS and Android with an offline mode that syncs when connectivity returns. Agrapp does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public web surface, commercial links, and domain security posture.

providers.name: MEQ Solutions
providers.description: MEQ Solutions is an Australian agrifood technology company delivering what it calls the world's only end-to-end measurement of red meat quality and yield. Its integrated hardware-and-software suite — MEQ Probe, MEQ Camera, MEQ Live, and MEQ Insights — gives producers, feedlots, processors, brands, retailers, and food-service operators objective, real-time carcass and eating-quality data. Deployed across Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and Brazil, MEQ has completed over 10 million scans across 60+ deployments and reports a demonstrated 10x ROI. The company is backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API surface is currently published; the meqinsights.com portal is a customer login.

providers.name: Apollo Agriculture
providers.description: Apollo Agriculture is an agricultural technology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, that helps small-scale farmers across Africa maximize their profits. Apollo delivers a full-stack service bundling quality farm inputs (seed and fertilizer), flexible input financing and credit, satellite- and machine-learning-driven agronomic advice, crop insurance, and market access, distributed through a network of local agrodealers and mobile technology. The company serves smallholder farmers in markets including Kenya and Zambia and is backed by investors including Anthemis and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile tracks Apollo Agriculture as a company in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: EZ Farming
providers.description: EZ Farming is an agriculture investment and farm-ownership platform that lets individuals start or co-own a working farm without doing the day-to-day work themselves. Members can buy land in the EZFarming farm estate, join a farmer cooperative to co-own a farm alongside other investors, buy produce directly from managed farms, or invest in agricultural projects for returns. Backed by 500 Global, the company packages land acquisition, farm management, and produce offtake into a single managed offering aimed at first-time farm owners and agriculture investors.

providers.name: Green Eye Technology
providers.description: Greeneye Technology is an agricultural technology company that builds AI-powered precision spraying systems for weed management. Its retrofit hardware and computer-vision software integrate into existing farm sprayers to identify weeds in real time and apply herbicide only where it is needed, enabling Green-on-Green (weed-versus-crop) and Green-on-Brown (bare-soil) selective application that can reduce herbicide use by up to 90 percent while performing species-level analysis to help combat herbicide resistance. The company positions its dual-line system as a way for growers to cut chemical costs, reduce soil contamination, and address the roughly $100 billion in annual crop losses attributed to weeds. Greeneye is a Techstars-backed company and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio; it currently publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: TreeX Robotics
providers.description: TreeX Robotics is an Israeli physical-AI company founded in 2024 that is bringing autonomous robotics to outdoor field operations at scale. TreeX replaces human field crews with fleets of physical AI-powered autonomous workers that perform high-skill field operations as an on-demand labor service, regardless of terrain or ground conditions. The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (seed, 2024) and operates in Israel, the United States, and Italy. TreeX publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Wheelocity
providers.description: Wheelocity (Wheelocity Fresh Private Limited) is a Bangalore, India based logistics and supply-chain company building daily fresh-produce and grocery delivery networks for underserved rural markets across India, which it frames as "the access rails for Bharat commerce." Its phygital (online plus offline) model combines location intelligence, IoT hardware, cold-chain and predictive demand forecasting with an electric-vehicle first-mile and last-mile fleet and a consumer app branded WoW. The company reports serving more than one million households, running over 100,000 km of EV movement daily and avoiding tens of thousands of kilograms of produce waste each day. Wheelocity is a venture-backed operating company (Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio) and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Agryco
providers.description: Agryco — trading as Agriconomie until its September 2024 rebrand — is a French online marketplace and e-commerce platform that sells agricultural supplies direct to farmers: mineral, organic and foliar fertilizers, conventional and organic seeds, phytosanitary products, animal nutrition and livestock equipment, plus tractor, spraying, harvesting and soil-working spare parts. Founded in 2014 by Clement Le Fournis, Dinh Nguyen and Paolin Pascot, the company operates a one-stop procurement site for professional farmers across France, Belgium, Germany, Spain and Italy, wrapping the catalog in advisory services (agronomy experts on the phone six days a week), fertilizer blending, equipment valuation and 60-day payment terms. It raised a EUR 60 million Series B in 2022 co-led by Treis Group, Temasek and Aliment Capital with Eurazeo participating, and publishes the Agrycomag technical magazine at agryco.com/blog. Agryco is an end-user commerce product: as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Lithos
providers.description: Lithos Carbon is a deep-tech carbon-removal company that spreads crushed basalt on croplands to accelerate enhanced rock weathering, converting atmospheric CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate that is permanently stored as ocean carbonates. The company pairs soil models and machine learning with agronomic partnerships to maximize durable carbon dioxide removal while improving soil health and crop productivity for farmers, and sells the resulting high-permanence carbon credits to corporate buyers. Surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; an enrichment pass confirmed the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface as of this profile.

providers.name: Propagate Ventures
providers.description: Propagate (formerly Propagate Ventures) is a regenerative-agriculture company founded in 2017 that helps farmland owners, farmers, and investors design, plant, finance, and manage agroforestry and tree-crop systems. Its flagship SaaS product, Overyield, lets farmers, developers, and investors model tree-crop economics, choose crops, and design tree-crop systems that work alongside existing farm operations. Propagate pairs the software with technical assessments, site prep and planting services, improved tree genetics, and ongoing project monitoring, and is a partner in the USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities. The company advises 30,000+ acres of agroforestry supporting over 760,000 trees and shrubs. Propagate publishes no public API or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Smallhold
providers.description: Smallhold is a specialty organic mushroom company founded in 2017 by Andrew Carter and Adam DeMartino and headquartered in Brooklyn, New York. A Certified B Corporation, Smallhold grows gourmet mushroom varieties — including blue oyster, lion's mane, maitake, royal trumpet, and shiitake — using modular, automated "minifarm" growing environments designed for distributed, locally grown supply to grocery retailers and restaurants. Its public presence is a direct-to-consumer and retail-partner storefront built on Shopify; the company publishes no first-party developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead and run through the enrichment pipeline, which confirmed no bespoke API surface — only Shopify's platform OAuth discovery documents are exposed on the shop domain.

providers.name: Grubmarket
providers.description: GrubMarket is a food technology company founded in 2014 that digitally transforms the American food supply chain across the U.S. and Canada. It operates a B2B wholesale eCommerce marketplace connecting buyers to thousands of food products, an AI-powered ERP and warehouse-management software suite (WholesaleWare) for food distributors and growers, and a direct-to-consumer farm-fresh food delivery service. Backed by Battery Ventures, GGV Capital, and Y Combinator, GrubMarket was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass GrubMarket publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Aerodyne
providers.description: Aerodyne Group is a Malaysia-headquartered DT3 (drone technology, data technology, and digital transformation) enterprise solutions provider, founded in 2014. Through its Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) model and the AI-powered, cloud-based vertikaliti asset-management platform, Aerodyne turns aerial and sensor data into deep analytics and actionable insights for infrastructure, power line, wind turbine, solar, and agricultural (Agrimor) asset inspection and management. Operating across 45 countries with a global network of AeroRangers, it was ranked the world's number-one drone service provider by Drone Industry Insights in 2021 and 2022. Aerodyne is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable specification has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Andes
providers.description: Andes (Andes Ag, Inc.) is a climate-technology and agricultural-biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Alameda, California. Andes engineers and selects beneficial soil microorganisms that are applied alongside seed in commodity row-crop production — corn, soybean, wheat and canola — where they accelerate the natural conversion of atmospheric carbon dioxide into stable soil inorganic carbon (carbonate minerals), a process the company calls Microbial Carbon Mineralization. Andes sells the resulting durable carbon dioxide removal as verified credits to corporate buyers and Scope 3 programs, and pays participating growers through the Andes Carbon Program. The company published the first Microbial Carbon Mineralization methodology, developed with EcoEngineers under ISO 14064, and has run field trials with Bayer, Cargill, Corteva, Nutrien and Wilbur-Ellis. Andes has raised roughly $38M, including a Series A co-led by Leaps by Bayer and Cavallo Ventures, and its shares trade on private secondary venues including EquityZen and Nasdaq Private Market. Andes publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Brumby
providers.description: Brumby (formerly GrazeMate) is a Y Combinator-backed (W2026) precision-grazing company based in Sydney, Australia, building an autonomous drone toolkit for cattle ranchers. Brumby drones plan routes and move herds with gentle, AI-guided pressure, fly scheduled monitoring missions that locate and count every animal, measure standing dry-matter pasture biomass from the air, and inspect water troughs, tanks and fences on every flight — all managed from a single phone app that works online or in a local base-station mode without connectivity. The company is running pilot programs and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is a company lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Inari
providers.description: Inari Agriculture, Inc. — "The SEEDesign company" — is a Cambridge, Massachusetts agricultural biotechnology company founded by Flagship Pioneering in 2016, with additional sites in West Lafayette, Indiana and Ghent, Belgium. Its SEEDesign platform combines genomics, artificial intelligence and predictive design with a multiplex gene-editing toolbox to accelerate crop improvement in soybean, corn and wheat, targeting 10-20% yield gains alongside roughly 40% reductions in nitrogen and water use. Inari runs a partner-first, business-to-business model, licensing designed seed to independent seed companies and breeders rather than selling to farmers directly. Inari publishes an llms.txt at inari.com/llms.txt but operates no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract; its data platform (Databricks-based) is internal. Not to be confused with the unrelated medical-device company Inari Medical.

providers.name: Universal Corporation
providers.description: Universal Corporation is a global leaf tobacco merchant and processor that selects, buys, processes, packs, stores, ships, and finances leaf tobacco for sale to manufacturers of consumer tobacco products. Operating in approximately 30 countries, Universal Corporation is the world's leading supplier of leaf tobacco, providing supply chain management, processing, and blending services. The company has developed digital platforms including MobiLeaf, a tablet-based grower management system for tobacco farmer support and crop tracking.

providers.name: Windfall Bio
providers.description: Windfall Bio transforms methane emissions into organic fertilizer and carbon credits using proprietary non-GMO methane-eating microbes (methanotrophs). The company operates across agriculture, coal mining, oil & gas, and waste management, capturing methane at the source and converting it into a soil amendment while generating verifiable carbon credits. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the latest enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Bindbridge
providers.description: Bindbridge is an AI-driven molecular discovery company founded in 2025 and based in Cambridge, UK, developing next-generation crop protection through targeted protein degradation. Its BRIDGE platform uses AI to discover and design molecular glues and targeted protein degraders with novel modes of action against weeds and crop diseases, combining AI candidate generation, computational docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and free-energy binding calculations to accelerate agricultural R&D across herbicides, insecticides, and fungicides. The company raised $3.8M to help reduce billion-dollar crop losses and is backed by Speedinvest. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; it publishes no public API or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Entocycle
providers.description: Entocycle is a London-based insect farming technology company building industrial-scale, controlled-environment facilities that use black soldier fly bioconversion to turn organic waste streams into insect protein for animal feed and organic fertilizer (frass). Its platform combines modular climate-controlled farm infrastructure, real-time AI-driven insect monitoring that counts and tracks insects across their lifecycle, and fully automated production systems to standardize output across deployments worldwide. Entocycle partners with waste management companies, agricultural producers, insect companies, and offtake buyers to develop and operate circular-economy insect farms. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Sunday
providers.description: Sunday (Sunday Lawn Care, getsunday.com) is a direct-to-consumer, subscription lawn and yard care brand. It builds a personalized annual plan for each customer's exact lot from satellite imagery, soil data, and local climate patterns, then ships pesticide-free, phosphorus-free fertilizer, weed control, grass seed, and pest-control products on a seasonal cadence. Plans include Sunny AI guidance and Yard Advisor expert support, plus regional lawn-care guides for 1,700+ US cities. Sunday is a consumer commerce company rather than an API provider: it publishes a machine-readable llms.txt for agents and runs an internal application API (api.getsunday.com), but exposes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documented API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Blue River Technology
providers.description: Blue River Technology is an agricultural robotics and machine-learning company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and a wholly owned subsidiary of John Deere (Deere & Company), which acquired it in 2017. Founded in 2011 by Jorge Heraud and Lee Redden out of Stanford University, the company builds intelligent machinery that combines computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and full-stack software to make farming more precise and sustainable. Its flagship product, See & Spray, uses onboard cameras and deep-learning models to distinguish crops from weeds in real time and target herbicide only where it is needed, dramatically reducing chemical use. Blue River operates as John Deere's autonomy and computer-vision engineering hub, applying the same perception and edge-AI stack across agriculture, construction, and mining equipment. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its technology ships embedded in John Deere machinery and is surfaced to growers through John Deere Operations Center rather than a standalone developer program.

providers.name: feld.energy
providers.description: feld.energy (Feld.Energy GmbH) is a Freising, Germany based Agri-PV (agrivoltaics) project developer and investment company that helps farmers and landowners install turnkey agricultural photovoltaic systems on their fields. It combines expertise from agriculture, energy, and project development to co-locate crop or livestock production with solar generation, offering landowners lease income, revenue sharing, or full-ownership models with state-secured grid feed-in over roughly 20 years. The company handles every step from land assessment and permitting through construction and operation. It reports 800+ partner farmers, 900+ hectares of projects, and 320+ MW of secured grid capacity. It is a portfolio company of HV Capital and is in the API Evangelist network as a climate-energy company profile; it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Mosa Meat
providers.description: Mosa Meat is a European food technology company headquartered in Maastricht, the Netherlands, founded in 2016 as a spin-off of Maastricht University by Mark Post and Peter Verstrate. The company develops cultivated (cell-cultured) beef using cellular agriculture: a small cell sample taken from a cow is nurtured through natural processes into muscle and fat tissue, which the company states can yield up to 80,000 burgers from a single sample. Mosa Meat produced the world's first cultured beef hamburger in 2013 and now operates the Mosa C.A.M.P.U.S. (Center for Advanced Meat Production, Upscaling, and Sustainability) in Maastricht, reported as the largest cultivated meat campus in the world. It is a B Corp certified organization pursuing regulatory approval and market entry for cultivated beef burgers. Mosa Meat is a laboratory and food production business; it publishes no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Sanderson Farms
providers.description: Sanderson Farms was the third-largest poultry producer in the United States, producing over 13 million chickens per week before being acquired by a joint venture of Cargill and Continental Grain in 2022 to form Wayne-Sanderson Farms. Headquartered in Laurel, Mississippi, the company operated processing facilities across the southeastern United States and was a Fortune 1000 company. As a large-scale agricultural and food production enterprise, Sanderson Farms does not offer public developer APIs. The company focused on poultry processing, supply chain management, and food safety operations.

providers.name: Seedsight
providers.description: Seedsight is a Porto, Portugal and Delaware, USA based agri-food technology company applying artificial intelligence and optical sensing to the cereal and grain value chain. Its platform helps farmers, traders, millers, and food processors make smarter, faster, and safer decisions through contaminant and safety screening, biological-fingerprinting traceability for origin and variety identification, Flour Extraction Rate yield prediction, and Flour Rheology quality prediction. Backed by Techstars, Seedsight raised roughly EUR 1.78M to reduce agri-food waste. At present the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and domain security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Agrostar
providers.description: AgroStar (Ulink Agritech Private Ltd) is a leading Indian agri-tech company on a mission to help farmers grow more and earn more, sustainably. Founded in Pune, it operates India's largest digital farmer network and agri-inputs platform, serving millions of farmers across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh through its Kisan (AgriDoctor) mobile app. AgroStar builds a connected ecosystem across the agricultural value chain — farm advisory, quality agri-inputs, omnichannel retail access and global market linkages — backed by data and agronomy expertise, with a focus on climate-smart agriculture, water conservation and reducing food waste. It is a portfolio company of Accel. AgroStar's public corporate site is Wix-powered and exposes a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint plus an /llms.txt for agentic AI access to public site content; it does not publish a developer-facing product API.

providers.name: Agvend
providers.description: AgVend is an agricultural technology company founded in 2017 (Austin, TX) that provides digital engagement and commerce software to agricultural retailers, cooperatives, manufacturers, and distributors. Its white-labeled Grower Portal (web and mobile) gives ag retailers a branded storefront, CRM, sales enablement, digital billing, and integrated payments, while its Nexus product extends the platform to manufacturers and distributors across the ag supply chain. The platform integrates with major ag and energy ERPs, agronomy planning tools, and grain and financing systems, and exposes an API Access Driver that lets customers pull structured platform data into external reporting and BI tools such as Power BI. Backed by 8vc and Tidemark.

providers.name: Pivot Bio
providers.description: Pivot Bio is an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Berkeley, California with additional operations in St. Louis, Missouri. The company engineers naturally occurring soil microbes to fix atmospheric nitrogen on crop root systems, providing a biological alternative to synthetic nitrogen fertilizer that reduces nitrous-oxide emissions, nitrate runoff, and exposure to volatile fertilizer prices. Pivot Bio's product line includes PROVEN 40 and PROVEN G3 (corn and corn silage), RETURN (wheat and small grains), CERT-N (cotton), and RETAIN (sorghum). The company also operates N-OVATOR, an outcomes-based program that pays farmers for verified emissions reductions; the program reports having paid out more than $6M to growers since 2022 and contributing to over 1,050,000 metric tons of CO2e avoided. Pivot Bio was founded by Karsten Temme (CEO) and Alvin Tamsir. Investors include Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Temasek, DCVC, Generation Investment Management, Pavilion Capital, G2 Venture Partners, Bond, and others. Pivot Bio's product is the microbe, not an API; the company operates a farmer-facing Salesforce-based portal but does not publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Ekomoditi
providers.description: eKomoditi (PT Ekomoditi Solutions Indonesia) is a Southeast Asian agriculture-technology company, founded in 2015 and based in Jakarta, that builds digital plantation-management software for oil palm, rubber, sugar, and durian estates. Its flagship Electronic Plantation Control System (ePCS) replaces paper-based field recording with a mobile in-field Android app, an eGIS geographic mapping application, mills automation, and business-intelligence analytics — capturing harvesting, fertilization, pest-management, worker, and transport data for same-day reporting, labor-fraud monitoring, quality control, and traceability. eKomoditi also offers aerial-mapping drone services, a plantation marketplace, and due-diligence consulting. The company is backed by 500 Global and ZB Capital. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: aardaia
providers.description: Aardaia is a Wageningen (Netherlands) agri-biotech startup that turns wild plant species into new commercial crops through accelerated domestication, combining classical plant breeding with modern genomics and AI rather than genetic modification. Its flagship is the aardaker, a nitrogen-fixing legume-tuber that yields a naturally protein-rich crop (roughly 10g protein per 100g of fresh tuber) without synthetic fertilizer. The company raised a EUR 5M seed round led by Point Nine in 2026. Aardaia does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a Point Nine portfolio lead.

providers.name: Central Coast Agriculture
providers.description: Central Coast Agriculture, Inc. (CCA) is a vertically integrated California cannabis cultivator and manufacturer headquartered in the Santa Ynez Valley north of Santa Barbara, best known for its Raw Garden brand of fresh-frozen concentrates, vapes and infused pre-rolls. The company describes itself as a progressive farm focused on utilizing science and sustainability to grow quality, modern crops, and operates its own farming, genetics/breeding and extraction programs. It is a physical agricultural and consumer-packaged-goods business: it publishes a corporate site, a consumer brand site and a wholesale ordering page, but no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: iChase Co., Ltd.
providers.description: iChase Co., Ltd. (iCHASE) builds AI-powered biosecurity and precision-farming systems for modern agriculture. Its integrated computer-vision monitoring platform protects livestock and optimizes growth for dairy, poultry, warehouse/industrial, and utility operations. Flagship products include the AI Bird Repeller, which detects birds in real time and deploys automated, chemical-free laser deterrence to reduce avian-flu and contamination risk, and InsightScale, which uses 3D scanning and AI weight prediction to track poultry Average Daily Gain and uniformity without stressful manual weighing. iCHASE is a member of the NVIDIA Inception program, a 2024 THRIVE Top 100 Global Innovator, and a 500 Global portfolio company. The site markets an "Open API" capability, but no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs were discoverable at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Pyka
providers.description: Pyka is an Alameda, California company that designs and manufactures large, dual-use heavy-lift autonomous electric aircraft for commercial and defense operations. Its flagship products are the Pelican 2 autonomous crop-protection aircraft for aerial application and the DropShip long-range heavy-lift cargo UAS. Pyka builds a fully integrated, vertically owned autonomy stack — an Autonomy Engine (real-time OS, sensor fusion, flight control, and path planning), a Mission Control operator suite (simulation, communications, and operator interface), and custom aerospace-grade hardware. The company is backed by DCVC and Obvious Ventures. Pyka does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint. Surfaced via VC portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: TRIC Robotics
providers.description: TRIC Robotics builds autonomous agricultural robots that replace chemical pesticides with ultraviolet light. Its flagship platform, Luna, is a tractor-scale robot that roams California strawberry fields after dark, using UV-C light to kill fungal pathogens such as powdery mildew and botrytis while a mechanical "Bug Vac" removes pests like Lygus bugs, spotted wing drosophila, and spider mites — without a single drop of pesticide. Founded in 2017 by Dr. Adam Stager and Vishnu Somasundaram out of the University of Delaware and now based in California, TRIC operates a robotics-as-a-service model that requires no upfront investment from growers, and reports pesticide reductions of up to 70% across the farms it serves. The company raised a $5.5M seed round led by Version One Ventures to expand its fleet across Santa Maria, Oxnard, and Watsonville. TRIC Robotics is an agricultural robotics operator and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Vegrow
providers.description: Vegrow is a Bengaluru-based B2B fruits marketplace founded in 2020 by IIT alumni that connects Indian fruit farmers with demand outlets across retail channels, using technology to match produce such as apples, bananas, pomegranates, and grapes with buyers, handling grading, sorting, quality assurance, and delivery, and paying farmers digitally. Backed by GIC, Prosus Ventures, Matrix Partners India, Elevation Capital, Lightspeed, and Ankur Capital, it raised a $46M round led by GIC in December 2023. Vegrow publishes no public API or developer program today.

providers.name: Deep Rooted
providers.description: Deep Rooted.Co is a direct-to-consumer fresh produce brand operated by Clover Ventures Pvt. Ltd, a Bengaluru-based agritech company founded in 2018 that launched the Deep Rooted consumer brand in 2020. The company works with a network of small-scale farmers using greenhouse and hydroponic techniques within roughly 150km of Bengaluru and Hyderabad, providing agronomy support from seed to harvest and delivering fruits, vegetables, Indian staples and greens, exotic produce and an easy-cook range direct to households the morning after ordering. Deep Rooted is backed by Accel. It sells through a consumer web storefront and mobile apps; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification, so this profile captures company identity and web properties only.

providers.name: Enko Chem
providers.description: Enko Chem, Inc. (Enko) is an agricultural life sciences company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Mystic, Connecticut, where it operates an 89,000 sq ft research lab and greenhouse campus. Enko discovers and develops next-generation crop protection chemistry — weed, disease, insect and soil-pest control — using its proprietary ENKOMPASS platform, which combines DNA-encoded library screening, structure-based design, artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify new modes of action and lead molecules faster and at lower cost than conventional agrochemical R&D. Enko works through partnerships with Syngenta, Bayer, Nufarm and the Gates Foundation Strategic Investment Fund rather than selling software, and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: The Andersons
providers.description: The Andersons, Inc. is a diversified agribusiness company headquartered in Maumee, Ohio, with operations in grain, plant nutrients, and renewables. Founded in 1947, the company operates grain elevators, fertilizer and nutrient businesses, and ethanol facilities across the United States and Canada. The Andersons does not publish a public developer API or developer portal. Business integrations are handled through EDI and direct partner arrangements.

providers.name: Vosbor
providers.description: Vosbor is a digital trading platform for bulk agricultural commodities, headquartered in Amsterdam with offices in Singapore and Shanghai. Founded in 2019 and backed by Lux Capital, its exchange lets trading firms and end users trade corn, wheat, soybean, palm oil and other grains and oilseeds in spot and forward markets, with integrated KYC, encrypted trade data, straight-through processing, and a WhatsApp AI broker that negotiates with multiple counterparties simultaneously. Market data is downloadable in CSV, and the company advertises data access through an API for customers, but publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Silo
providers.description: Silo is a cloud-based ERP platform built specifically for the fresh-produce supply chain, serving growers, packers, shippers, and distributors. The platform unifies produce operations across five modules - a diversified produce ERP, labor and asset management, payments and financial operations, EDI and traceability, and analytics and intelligence - to improve operational efficiency and financial visibility for small to midsize produce businesses. Silo is backed by a16z and Initialized Capital. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: AgroMatch
providers.description: AgroMatch is a Chilean agricultural technology (AgTech) platform, founded in 2018 and backed by 500 Global, that connects farmers, agricultural contractors, and machinery owners in a single collaborative marketplace. Often described as the "Airbnb of agricultural machinery," it lets machinery owners lease idle equipment (tractors, implements, portable bins) during low-use periods to farmers in regions whose seasons do not coincide, and lets farmers contract or offer agricultural services such as harvesting, soil preparation, and crop applications. The platform also supports buying and selling new and used machinery, operative leasing, and supplier networking, using artificial intelligence and IoT to match demand for machinery with available supply. AgroMatch reports more than 400 B2B customers across Chile and Perú with operations extending to the US, Colombia, and Mexico. The company operates as a web and mobile application at app.agromatch.cl; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: BioConsortia
providers.description: BioConsortia, Inc. is an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Davis, California, with additional laboratories in New Zealand, that discovers and commercializes microbial biologicals for row crops and specialty agriculture. Its patented Advanced Microbial Selection (AMS) process, RhizoViz microbe-visualization tool and GenePro genomics and gene-engineering platform are used to screen a collection of more than 60,000 characterized microorganisms — including roughly 9,000 endophytes — into nitrogen-fixation biofertilizers, biocontrol products (bionematicides and biofungicides) and biostimulants, largely delivered as seed treatments. The company sells physical crop inputs through partners such as Mosaic, Nichino America and Envu; its platform technologies are internal R&D instruments rather than commercial software, and BioConsortia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Nofence
providers.description: Nofence is a Norwegian agritech company (founded 2011, headquartered in Batnfjordsøra, Norway) that produces the world's first commercial virtual fencing system for livestock. Solar-powered GPS collars worn by cattle, sheep and goats keep animals inside virtual pastures that farmers draw on a map, with the collar teaching animals boundaries through audio cues before a mild electric pulse. The system is operated entirely from a mobile app (iOS and Android) and a web portal, communicating over GPS and the cellular network with no base stations or buried wire. Farmers get real-time animal location, boundary/escape push notifications, herd replay, grazing-history and multi-species management. Nofence is a consumer/farmer-facing product: as of this profile it publishes a mobile app and web portal but no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface. It is a portfolio company of Speedinvest, added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.

providers.name: Qarbotech
providers.description: Qarbotech (Qarbotech Sdn Bhd) is a Malaysian agritech and nanotechnology company that develops biocompatible organic compounds to optimize plant photosynthesis and raise agricultural productivity. Its flagship product, QarboGrow, is a photosynthesis-enhancing treatment marketed to boost photosynthetic efficiency and lift crop yields by roughly 20-30% while improving plant health, disease resistance, and crop quality, alongside the Harvast and Harvast+ product lines. Headquartered in Puchong, Selangor with additional offices in Bukit Mertajam, Penang and Jakarta, Indonesia, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. Qarbotech is a physical-product agritech business and publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Synphony
providers.description: Synphony builds and deploys robots that work in the real world, combining AI, robotics, and human-in-the-loop systems so machines can perform practical physical tasks across agriculture, assembly, and inspection. Its platform trains AI models on real-world data, tests robot performance in realistic scenarios, and deploys systems into production. The company's first application is autonomous strawberry-harvesting robots plus farm software services (bed-level analytics, data-pipeline integration, and agentic solutions), targeting California's roughly $3B strawberry industry where labor is about 60% of costs. Founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), Synphony runs a customer-facing platform at app.synphony.co but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: CHS Inc.
providers.description: CHS Inc. is a Fortune 500 diversified, integrated, global agricultural cooperative owned by farmers, ranchers, cooperatives, and individual producers. Headquartered in Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota, CHS describes itself as the largest farmer-owned cooperative in the United States, with more than 750 member cooperatives, 75,000+ individual producer-owners, and 20,000+ preferred stockholders. The cooperative serves customers in 65 countries through three primary business divisions: Agriculture (crop nutrients, crop protection, precision agriculture, seed, animal nutrition, and oilseed products), Energy (refined fuels, propane, lubricants, pipelines, terminals, and renewable fuels under the Cenex brand), and Services (hedging, payment solutions, transportation, and capital services). Major brands include Cenex, Allegiant (seed), Payback (animal nutrition), and N-Edge (crop nutrients). CHS does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are provided through digital platforms such as MyCHS (online portal for grain tickets, billing, and payments) and CHS Connect (digital self-service for crop protection and energy wholesale customers).

providers.name: Orchard Robotics
providers.description: Orchard Robotics (Orchard AI, "The AI Farming Company") is an agricultural technology startup founded in 2022 that builds AI-powered camera systems and farm-management software for precision fruit and vine growing. Its FruitScope platform mounts AI-enabled cameras on any farm vehicle to collect precise per-tree and per-vine data — fruit count, size, color, and growth rate — which is stored in FruitScope Vault and surfaced through FruitScope OS for crop decision-making, with a Vineyard Robotics division serving grape growers. Backed by General Catalyst, the company has raised roughly $22M. As of this profile Orchard Robotics publishes a marketing and careers website but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Rabobank
providers.description: Rabobank is a Dutch multinational banking and financial services company organized as a cooperative with a strong focus on the food and agriculture sector. It serves retail, business, corporate, and wholesale customers in the Netherlands and operates a global Food & Agribusiness practice through Rabobank Wholesale & Rural and the Rabobank Group internationally. Rabobank publishes a developer portal at docs.developer.rabobank.com (legacy URL developer.rabobank.nl redirects there) exposing PSD2-mandated open banking APIs (Account Information, Payment Initiation, Funds Confirmation) as well as Premium / Beyond-PSD2 commercial APIs for corporate cash management and notifications, with sandbox endpoints for development and a regulated production tier under PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication. Underlying schemes are aligned with the Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 XS2A Framework.

providers.name: Haseel
providers.description: Haseel (حصيل) is a Riyadh-based technology startup, founded in 2018, that delivers fresh fruits and vegetables to consumers across Saudi Arabia through its iOS and Android mobile apps. The company sources high-quality produce and fulfills each order from the nearest of its branches inside Riyadh, pairing a curated selection with fast, reliable last-mile delivery. Haseel reports more than 400,000 app downloads, three branches inside Riyadh, and over 1,000 orders per day, and is backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Haseel is a consumer produce-delivery app and does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Kuehnle AgroSystems
providers.description: Kuehnle AgroSystems, Inc. (KAS) is a Honolulu, Hawaii microalgae biotechnology company founded in 2007 by Dr. Adelheid "Heidi" Kuehnle, with a second site in Cork, Ireland. KAS produces high-value natural products from microalgae for the food, feed and health markets using a patented heterotrophic "dark fermentation" process and proprietary non-GMO Hawaiian algal strains that run in standard fermentation equipment rather than open ponds or photobioreactors, compressing production from weeks to days with substantially lower cost, land, water and energy use. Its lead products are natural astaxanthin and algal protein, sold into nutraceuticals, cosmetics and skincare, functional foods and beverages, and aquaculture and animal feed; in August 2025 KAS entered a development and commercialization partnership with Corbion for an esterified natural astaxanthin. KAS sells ingredients, strains and fermentation process technology rather than software: it publishes no API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable contract, and kuehnleagro.com is a six-page Squarespace marketing site.

providers.name: Poultry sync
providers.description: PoultrySync is an AI-powered data management platform for the poultry value chain, helping producers increase productivity and reduce errors across broilers, breeders, hatchery, layers, slaughterhouse, feedmill, grandparents, lab, and quality management. The platform automates data collection, provides real-time dashboards, detects anomalies, forecasts production, and supports compliance reporting and audits, integrating with existing ERP systems in days. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Ohalo Genetics
providers.description: Ohalo Genetics is an American agricultural biotechnology company founded in 2019 and led by CEO David Friedberg, developing plant-breeding platforms and proprietary crop varieties. Its flagship Boosted Breeding technology — marketed as "2x + 2x = 4x" — alters the reproductive circuitry of parent plants so each parent passes its entire genome to the next generation rather than a random half, producing polyploid offspring that carry the full genetic contribution of both parents and, in early field trials, substantially higher yields. Ohalo pairs this with an Agile Breeding service and a True Seed program that ships uniform, disease-free seedlings directly to growers, with active programs in potato, almond (the FruitionOne self-fertile Nonpareil variety), strawberry and corn, delivered through partnerships such as the Allied Potato partnership and a strawberry consortium. The company sells plant genetics and breeding services to agricultural partners; it is not a software vendor and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: AgZen
providers.description: AgZen is an MIT spinout building RealCoverage, a sensor- and AI-based system that measures and controls how many droplets of crop-protection product land on every leaf during agricultural spraying. A boom-mounted computer-vision sensor analyzes spray coverage and droplet quality in real time and displays actionable data on an in-cab tablet, automatically optimizing foliar sprays on any sprayer as the operator drives. Growers use RealCoverage to cut chemical and water use by up to 50% while maintaining or improving efficacy and yield, with a typical payback in under a year. RealCoverage retrofits onto any generation of sprayer and won Crop Protection Solution of the Year in 2025. AgZen is headquartered at Greentown Labs in Somerville, Massachusetts and is backed by DCVC Bio, Material Impact, Astanor Ventures, and Syngenta Group Ventures.

providers.name: Iron Ox
providers.description: Iron Ox (legally Inevitable Tech, Inc.) was a San Carlos, California robotics company that built autonomous indoor farms — hydroponic greenhouses worked by mobile transport robots and a robotic arm that seeded, moved, imaged and harvested leafy greens and herbs, with machine learning used to spot pests and disease plant by plant. Founded in 2015 by Brandon Alexander and Jon Binney, it went through Y Combinator (W16), raised roughly $98 million in total including a $53 million Series C led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures in September 2021, and ran greenhouses in Gilroy, California and Lockhart, Texas. It cut about half its staff — roughly 50 people — in November 2022 and ceased operations in mid-2023. Iron Ox never ran a developer program: it sold produce, not software, and the only public code it ever shipped was internal ROS robotics tooling on GitHub. Its site, ironox.com, is now a GoDaddy parking lander and every developer subdomain has been removed from DNS, so there is no API, specification, SDK or documentation surface left to profile.

providers.name: Kuva Space
providers.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth.
